newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: U.S. gives 257 mln rand for S.African development.
newsitem.headline: U.S. gives 257 mln rand for S.African development.

text.p: The United States signed a deal on Wednesday giving South Africa 256.7 million rand of aid to help fund development projects.
The aid will support 11 government programmes, most of which are already receiving U.S. aid as part of previous donations.
The cash brings total U.S. aid to South Africa in 1996 to 821 million rand, and is the final tranche of 2.7 billion rand pledged by U.S. president Bill Clinton for the period 1994-96.
U.S. ambassador James Joseph said the donation would help cement ties between the U.S. and South Africa.
The money will be ploughed into educational and development projects ranging from building new housing to supplying clean water.

The biggest single donation is 49 million rand to boost health care services. Other large projects include 48.9 million rand to fund basic education and 35 million rand for the tertiary education system.
The cash will be distributed through U.S. government body the United States Agency for International Development (USAID).

Aaron Williams, USAID director for South Africa, said more aid would be forthcoming next year. "..we anticipate carrying on our strong programme in South Africa now and for the foreseeable future," he said.
South African deputy finance minister Gill Marcus said the aid added to a wave of investment by U.S. companies returning to the country after disinvesting during the apartheid era.

On Monday U.S. tyre giant Goodyear Tire and Rubber Co reinvested with a $121 million deal after leaving in 1989. Owens Corning and drugs group American Home Products have also returned in the last two months.
Marcus said more such deals would follow and stressed the important role of private sector and government partnership in encouraging economic development.
